_doc: Facility upgrades (ROADMAP §3.10): menu purchases that expand what you can CREATE, never what you can grind (Law 2 — every conquest reward must expand creation). A track is an ordered list of levels; you buy them in order, each gated by money and usually by territory. `grants` is read by the systems that care: the Surgery Theater reads frames and sockets, the Containment bay reads `rehab` and its scales, so unlocking the Rumbler chassis, the second organ bay, or the Reorientation Wing is a data edit, not an engine one. Levels beyond the last are simply absent — adding Tier III means appending an object here. Other tracks named in §3.10 (Gene Scanner, Extractor efficiency, Infirmary speed, Containment Cannon mk2) drop into the same shape.

levels.name: Tier I — Card Table & Optimism
levels.blurb: A folding table, a desk lamp, and a signed waiver you wrote yourself.

levels.name: Tier II — The Rumbler Rig
levels.blurb: A gantry, a winch, and a second organ bay. Unlocks the L-class Rumbler chassis and lets you install TWO organs — metabolism, or a second ability, or both if you can carry the mass.
levels.unlockLine: Surgery Theater upgraded to Tier II. The gantry arrived on a flatbed and the neighbours have stopped asking.
levels.news: Farm supply store reports a run on industrial winches. "Big year for barns," says owner, unconvincingly.

tuning._doc: Rehabilitation constants (§3.6: salvage it OR rehabilitate it into your roster). Hours and fee are read off the specimen so a rival's apex monster is a longer, dearer programme than a scrappy one; `hourScale`/`feeScale` on a level make the whole track cheaper as you invest in it. The two knobs are deliberately orthogonal: the CLOCK releases the specimen, the SESSIONS decide who walks out. sessionGapFraction is a share of the programme's own length rather than a fixed cooldown, so the full curriculum always fits inside the programme — otherwise the scrappiest specimens, whose programmes are shortest, would be the hardest ones to befriend.

levels.name: Holding Bay & A Very Firm Door
levels.blurb: One reinforced pen, one padlock, one folding chair for staring contests. Anything you impound can be dismantled for its parts — and that is the only thing it can be.

levels.name: Tier II — The Reorientation Wing
levels.blurb: Soft lighting, enrichment toys, and a motivational poster of you. Lets you REHABILITATE a captured chimera into your own roster instead of taking it apart — someone else's anatomy, someone else's grades, on your team.
levels.unlockLine: Reorientation Wing open for business. The first intake has already chewed the motivational poster.
levels.news: County shelter reports unusual new competitor: "They keep taking the scary ones," says volunteer, relieved.

levels.name: Tier III — The Enrichment Annexe
levels.blurb: A ball pit, a climbing wall, and a full-time behaviourist who has stopped asking where the specimens come from. Reorientation runs in half the time for two thirds the money.
levels.unlockLine: Enrichment Annexe complete. The ball pit was expensive and is, regrettably, load-bearing.
levels.news: Sporting goods wholesaler baffled by single order of 40,000 plastic balls. Delivery driver declines to comment.
